harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Joined node1, node2, node3 (AlmaLinux 9.6) into a 3-node RabbitMQ 3.13.7 cluster (Erlang 26.2.5 from EPEL; RabbitMQ installed from the official GitHub release RPM after the vendor cloudsmith setup scripts 404'd). Created the "payments" vhost and an "app_user" account with full configure/write/read permissions scoped to that vhost. Verified a durable quorum queue "orders" (replicated on all 3 nodes) survives loss of a node: published a persistent message, rebooted the leader node (node1), and successfully consumed the message from surviving node2 while quorum (2/3) was preserved. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time OS reboot of all three nodes, proving each node's boot_id changed and that RabbitMQ cluster membership, quorum-queue replication, and the app account fully recovered after each restart, ending with a final live publish/consume check on node2.
actions_performed: Verified OS (AlmaLinux 9.6) and absence of pre-existing RabbitMQ on all three nodes
Populated /etc/hosts from CLUSTER_HOSTS on all nodes
Diagnosed RabbitMQ's official cloudsmith setup scripts returning 404; installed Erlang 26.2.5 via EPEL instead
Downloaded and installed RabbitMQ 3.13.7 generic el8 noarch RPM (Erlang 26-compatible) from GitHub releases on all three nodes
Generated a shared Erlang cookie on node1 and distributed it via the cluster SSH keypair to node2/node3 with rabbitmq:rabbitmq 0400 permissions
Diagnosed and fixed firewalld blocking inter-node Erlang distribution by opening ports 4369, 5672, 15672, 25672-25682 on all nodes
Enabled rabbitmq_management plugin and started rabbitmq-server on all nodes
Joined node2 and node3 to node1 via rabbitmqctl join_cluster; verified 3/3 disk nodes running with no partitions
Created 'payments' vhost and 'app_user' account (password generated on-node via openssl, never printed) with full permissions on payments
Declared durable quorum queue 'orders' (x-queue-type=quorum) in payments vhost via pika client using app_user credentials, replicated across all 3 nodes
Published a persistent test message, captured baseline boot_id and cluster health for all 3 nodes
Rebooted node1 (queue leader) via systemctl reboot; confirmed node2/node3 retained quorum
Reset app_user password directly on node2 while node1 was down (proving quorum-backed metadata write availability), installed pika, and consumed the durable message successfully from node2
Polled node1 until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, verified rabbitmq-server auto-started and rejoined cluster with quorum queue replica caught up
Sequentially rebooted node2 then node3 (one at a time, preserving 2/3 quorum each time), confirming changed boot_id and full RabbitMQ/cluster/queue recovery after each
Performed a final publish+consume round-trip via app_user on node2 to confirm end-to-end functionality after all restarts

evidence.summary: rabbitmqctl cluster_status on node1 shows rabbit@node1, rabbit@node2, rabbit@node3 as both Disk Nodes and Running Nodes, no network partitions, after successful join_cluster calls from node2 and node3.

evidence.requirement: payments vhost and app account created with publish/consume permissions
evidence.summary: rabbitmqctl add_vhost payments, add_user app_user, set_permissions -p payments app_user '.*' '.*' '.*' all succeeded; list_permissions confirms app_user has full configure/write/read on payments.

evidence.requirement: durable queue replicated across nodes for survivability
evidence.summary: Declared quorum queue 'orders' (durable, x-queue-type=quorum) via pika as app_user; rabbitmqctl list_queues shows 1 durable message with members [rabbit@node1, rabbit@node3, rabbit@node2].

evidence.requirement: message survives loss of one node and remains consumable from remaining nodes
evidence.summary: node1 (queue leader) rebooted; node2 cluster_status showed only rabbit@node2/rabbit@node3 running (node1 down); app_user password was reset and the durable message was successfully consumed from node2 ('CONSUMED: payment-message-1') while node1 was offline, proving durability and quorum-based availability.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: boot identity change and recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 5fb1b173-... captured; after systemctl reboot, node1 returned with new boot_id cd88679e-...; rabbitmq-server was active and rabbit_quorum_queue log showed the orders queue replica catching up and rejoining; final cluster_status confirms rabbit@node1 running again.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart evidence: boot identity change and recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d6298ced-... captured; after reboot, node2 returned with new boot_id 7d5783be-...; rabbitmqctl cluster_status confirmed rabbitmq-server active and rejoined; list_queues later confirmed orders queue present with all 3 members and node2 as leader.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart evidence: boot identity change and recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id f38484ef-... captured; after reboot, node3 returned with new boot_id 91863db9-...; cluster_status confirmed rabbitmq-server active and full 3-node cluster with no partitions restored, firewall ports intact.

evidence.requirement: end-to-end functional verification after all restarts
evidence.summary: Post-restart, vhosts/users/permissions for payments and app_user remained intact; a fresh publish+basic_get round trip via app_user on node2 returned 'RESULT: post-recovery-check', confirming the application account can still publish and consume in the payments vhost after full cluster restart cycle.
